function.name: SET_FPS
function.param: Maximum number of frames that Fenix can jump (not to draw) so that the speed of game gets the value of fps specified.
function.abstract: It establishes the speed of game

description.p: This function establishes the number of frames that must be completed and visualized per second. If this function is not used, the number of per second by default is 25.

Although your game will be executed in a variety of computers, faster than others, are desirable that the game works at the same speed in all of them. In order to obtain this effect, Fenix uses an internal limit of frames per second that you can choose with this function. When a computer is very fast and can execute all the processes and draw the screen in less time of the necessary one, Fenix will make a pause after the drawing so that drawn the total number of frames in a second is not superior to the established one at the most. However, when a computer is too slow and he is not able to show that number of frames in a second, Fenix will let draw some of them although yes it will execute the processes. This has the effect of which the animation is more abrupt, but in return the calculations of position and movement will be such that in a faster computer. Se te permite establecer un límite al número de frames consecutivos que Fenix puede saltarse: ese es el significado del segundo parámetro de esta función. Normally 1 or 2 is enough, and a high value can make that the game can not be played. If you want to use a value 0, so that the game slows down in slower computers, but the animation never is more abrupt.

It is advised to choose an amount of frames per second that the run time of frame is splitter of 60, since many monitors show by defect that number of images per second. To establish a superior number usually is to squander the resources of the computer, since the monitor will not be able to show these images, nor the user to distinguish them.
If you use this function with this parameters: SET_FPS(0,0), Fenix will run your game at top speed that the computer can. This is useful to obtain a benchmark of your game in a computer.

function.note: Of course, not all the computers are configured to a refreshment frequency of 60Hz, specially in graph modes of low resolution that you will use in Fenix. However it is a minimum value, and in any case few people can distinguish 60 images per second or more.
